arguments.reason:
Segments NL1-NL13 establish: root initial entry into InitialState, branching from InitialState to HighwayMode/UrbanMode with guards, HighwayMode internal substates and transitions (enter_hwy initial entry, cruise/lane_change alternatives, lane_change returning to cruise or exiting highway, cruise transitions, HighwayMode termination to FinishState), UrbanMode internal substates and transitions (enter_urban initial entry, three alternatives, lane_change_urban alternatives, straight alternatives, UrbanMode termination to FinishState), a dynamic cross-mode transition capability between HighwayMode and UrbanMode, and an independent collision-avoidance subsystem with its own initial entry and bidirectional transitions. Contracts split containment, initial-entry, transition endpoints (as groups plus per-alternative endpoint contracts), guard-disjointness where alternatives are guarded, and termination contracts. No fabricated cardinality, region, or progress contracts are added beyond what NL explicitly requires.</reason>

response.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequences of the closed FCSTM: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, dead-end/frontier facts, and stable termination. The CollisionAvoidanceSystem composite and its two states are declared but structurally unreachable from the top-level machine root ([*] -> AutonomousMode only; no edge from root or AutonomousMode reaches CollisionAvoidanceSystem), which converts the NL12 initial_entry and NL12/NL13 transition_endpoint obligations into operationally dead-end obligations, and makes the NL12 pedestrian/collision event and NL13 recovery event undeliverable in practice despite declared consumer transitions. Separately, FinishState is a reachable leaf with zero outgoing transitions, which is consistent with the NL6/NL10 termination obligations (FinishState acting as a true sink is expected for a termination state) so no termination candidate is warranted there. The HighwayMode<->UrbanMode dynamic-shift transitions (NL11) are realized via route-token macro edges verified reachable, so they are satisfied. All per-transition endpoint contracts inside CollisionAvoidanceSystem have their edges present in inventory (S2 would find the edge exists), so the defect is not a missing edge but an unreachable scope/owner and unreachable event consumers -- this requires a derived reachability contract at the composite scope, not rewriting the existing endpoint/init contracts.

Separately, FinishState is a reachable leaf with zero outgoing transitions, which is consistent with the NL6/NL10 termination obligations (FinishState acting as a true sink is expected for a termination state) so no termination candidate is warranted there. All per-transition endpoint contracts inside CollisionAvoidanceSystem have their edges present in inventory (S2 would find the edge exists), so the defect is not a missing edge but an unreachable scope/owner and unreachable event consumers -- this requires a derived reachability contract at the composite scope, not rewriting the existing endpoint/init contracts.
